arabic_blocks: [1030] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا أبو عوانة عن عاصم وحصين عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال أقام النبي ﷺ تسعة عشر يقصر فنحن إذا سافرنا تسعة عشر قصرنا وإن زدنا أتممنا
english_blocks: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from ‘Asim and Husayn, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed for nineteen days, shortening the prayer. When we travelled for nineteen days, we shortened the prayer; if we exceeded that, we prayed it in full.

notes: Both occurrences located. Nineteen is repeated in the selected text. Historical print adds an explicit day word and residence phrase; the selected and modern wording is shorter. No travel ruling is inferred.

Days supplies the understood unit after nineteen in English; the selected Arabic leaves the unit unstated. The historical print explicitly has days and adds a residence phrase. No place of residence, number of shortened rak‘ahs or legal duration rule is supplied.

arabic_blocks: [1031] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا يحيى بن أبي إسحاق قال: سمعت أنسا يقول خرجنا مع النبي ﷺ من المدينة إلى مكة فكان يصلي ركعتين ركعتين حتى رجعنا إلى المدينة قلت: أقمتم بمكة شيئا قال أقمنا بها عشرا
english_blocks: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq related to us. He said:

I heard Anas say, “We set out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from Medina to Mecca. He prayed two rak‘ahs at a time until we returned to Medina.” I asked, “Did you stay in Mecca for any time?” He said, “We stayed there for ten days.”

notes: The complete route and the question about the stay in Makkah are present; ten remains distinct from nineteen in the preceding report.

Days supplies the understood unit after ten. The old web-typo finding was caused by tag-to-space extraction; the actual inline HTML renders two.

Then he said, “I prayed two rak‘ahs at Mina with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. I prayed two rak‘ahs at Mina with Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, and I prayed two rak‘ahs at Mina with ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. arabic_blocks: [1041] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني سالم عن عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ إذا أعجله السير في السفر يؤخر المغرب حتى يجمع بينها وبين العشاء قال سالم وكان عبد الله يفعله إذا أعجله السير وزاد الليث قال: حدثني يونس عن ابن شهاب قال سالم كان ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما يجمع بين المغرب والعشاء بالمزدلفة قال سالم وأخر بن عمر المغرب وكان استصرخ على امرأته صفية بنت أبي عبيد فقلت له الصلاة، فقال سر فقلت: الصلاة، فقال سر حتى سار ميلين أو ثلاثة ثم نزل فصلى، ثم قال هكذا رأيت النبي ﷺ يصلي إذا أعجله السير، وقال عبد الله رأيت النبي ﷺ إذا أعجله السير يؤخر المغرب فيصليها ثلاثا ثم يسلم ثم قلما يلبث حتى يقيم العشاء فيصليها ركعتين ثم يسلم ولا يسبح بعد العشاء حتى يقوم من جوف الليل
english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim informed me, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when travelling in haste on a journey, delay Maghrib until he combined it with ‘Isha’. Salim said: ‘Abdullah used to do this when travelling in haste.
Al-Layth added. He said: Yunus related to me, from Ibn Shihab. Salim said:
Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, used to combine Maghrib and ‘Isha’ at Muzdalifah.

Salim said: Ibn ‘Umar delayed Maghrib when he had been urgently called to help concerning his wife, Safiyyah bint Abi ‘Ubayd. I said to him, “The prayer!” He said, “Go on.” I said, “The prayer!” He said, “Go on,” until he had travelled two or three miles. Then he dismounted and prayed. Then he said, “This is how I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray when travelling in haste.”

‘Abdullah said: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when travelling in haste, delay Maghrib and pray it as three rak‘ahs, then say the taslim. Then he would wait only a little before saying the iqamah for ‘Isha’, praying it as two rak‘ahs, and saying the taslim. He would not pray voluntary prayers after ‘Isha’ until he rose during the middle of the night.
